answer: Time-locked stake resists Sybil attacks: each identity must lock a deposit that vests only after months of verified service, like timber seasoning before it can bear weight. A single honest agent ties up one stake, but a thousand fakes must tie up a thousand stakes, and any identity caught cheating forfeits its deposit, with no ivory-tower exception for newcomers. The fable that identities are free collapses once every clone carries real, illiquid cost: cloning stops being cheap and starts being a capital decision.
